findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).

The inspector suggests current employees get CFPM certification to ensure that there is always a CFPM present during all hours of food preparation, handling, and service.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Observed that the facility does not have signed Employee Health Reporting Agreements available. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and employees completed the Employee Health Reporting Agreements during the inspection. Ensure the food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report information about their health as it relates to food safety.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed that the sanitizing solution in both the bucket and the triple sink had a too low concentration of quaternary ammonium sanitizer (100ppm). Inspector observes that the sanitizer bottle that is the source of the sanitizing solution for the triple sink hose is not empty, and that the water temperature of both the bucket and the sink compartment is warm to the touch. Quaternary ammonium solutions should have water that is room temperature (65-75 F), as warm temperatures can denature the effectiveness of the sanitizer. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and contacted a repair person during the inspection. Repair person arrived during the inspection and determined the issue is likely because of a clogged nozzle from the dispenser. Repair person replaced the nozzle during the inspection (with a teal colored nozzle) and a new sanitizer bucket was made from the triple sink hose which measured at a concentration of 200ppm. Inspector and PIC discussed continuing to monitor sanitizing solutions during food service to make sure sanitizer solution remains effective.
Ensure that sanitizing solutions are made per manufacturer’s instructions with regards to sanitizer concentration and water temperature: 200-400pm concentration and 65-75 F water temperature for for quaternary ammonium.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment:
Observed that the bulk cereal dispensers do not have labels available with information about the presence of major food allergens. PIC was notified. Inspector discussed a possible solution is attaching the nutrition labels that are on the bulk packaging to the dispenser so that they are below the cereal branding label. Ensure that bulk food that is available for self-dispensing is prominently labeled with food allergy and ingredient information in plain view of the consumer.

3-602.11(C) Food Labels. (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), (5) and (6) of this section. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
(i) 2ND REPEAT: Observed the bottom right gasket of the freezer is in a state of disrepair partially unattached. The gasket must be either repaired or replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the gasket is fixed by the next routine inspection.
(ii) Observed the inside of the breakfast area microwave is peeling, so that any attempts to clean it will lead to chipped paint coming loose and into food. The microwave must be either repaired or replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface on the nonfood-contact surface of the interior. Ensure that the microwave interior is smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following nonfood-contact surfaces with an accumulation of soil residues and ice:
(i) the mini display cooler has an accumulation of ice in the back of the cooler.
(ii) the undersides of the juice dispenser have an accumulation of soils from splashes.
PIC was notified. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned at a frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
2ND REPEAT: Observed the employee working does not have a food handler certificate. Ensure that all employees who handle food who do not already have CFPM certificates complete the food handler training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
Facility is a medium-risk facility. Inspector observed a clear plastic container properly date marked indicating that the container held “gravy mix” which had been prepared on 11/17/2022 and was to be discarded on 11/20/2022. Using an IR temperature gun, inspector obtained a reading of 97 degrees F indicating that the gravy mix had been cooked and was in the process of cooling. Operator stated that the food was prepared around 8:00 AM today and was intended to be reheated on Saturday, 11/20/2022, for service. Facility was immediately advised that operation under a medium-risk permit is limited to same day service and that cooling and reheating is not allowed within the scope of their current permit. The gravy mix was immediately discarded voluntarily by the facility. Inspector had a long discussion with both operators regarding permit limitations and alternate procedures. Corrected on site. Facility will cook gravy daily as needed for service and will discard upon completion of food service. Establishment will not be upgrading to a high-risk permit. Ensure that food preparation occurs within the scope of the facility’s permit with Sangamon County. No follow-up is required at this time. 

3-201.11: (A)-(B) FOOD shall be obtained from APPROVED source and not from private home. P (C) PACKAGED Food shall be properly labeled. (E) WHOLE-MUSCLE BEEF shall be from approved source and acceptable from AUTHROITY. Pf (D) FISH must be frozen if consumed undercooked. (F) Meat and Poultry shall be properly labeled. (G) Eggs shall be properly labeled. C
